hub.desc: Better sleep, less stress or lucid dreams: choose your goal and discover the meditations, worlds and tools that get you there. Free, no ads, no account.
hub.h1: Meditation for every goal: choose your path
hub.intro: Some people open a meditation app to fall asleep. Others want to calm a racing mind, learn the basics or set off on a shamanic journey. Whatever brings you here, MeditaDream has a path for it. Choose one of the 14 goals below to see the sessions to start with, the immersive worlds to visit and the features that help along the way. All 129 meditations are free, with no ads and no account, and they work offline once downloaded.

01.seo: How to Fall Asleep Faster: A Free Sleep App With No Ads
01.desc: Wondering how to fall asleep? Try sleep meditations that end without waking you, and sleep sounds that fade out on a timer. No subscription, no ads.
01.h1: How MeditaDream helps you sleep better
01.accroche: Fall asleep more peacefully: slow down your thoughts and let your body go.
pitch: Wondering how to fall asleep when your mind won’t slow down? MeditaDream gives you a sleep meditation made for bed, lights off. Drifting into Sleep guides you down gently and never wakes you at the end, so you can drift off before it finishes. On longer nights, Sleep Journey stays with you for 27 minutes, without any pressure to fall asleep.

Rather hear no words at all? Pick sleep sounds such as waves, forest or a mountain stream, set the timer from 5 to 60 minutes, and the sound fades out on its own. Choose your voice, slow it to 0.75×, then download everything once. In airplane mode, your sessions keep playing, with no network to disturb you.

Your evening can start winding down earlier, too. Precise Gratitude ends the day on something you enjoyed, Your Instant Refuge brings a reassuring place to mind, and the Oracle suggests three meditations for how you feel tonight. You can even write your own bedtime session and hear your phone read it aloud.
etapes: Half an hour before bed, open the Oracle and type how you feel, like “tired but wired.” Pick one of its three suggestions, or a short session like Precise Gratitude.
Lights off, start Drifting into Sleep or Sleep Journey. Both are made to be heard in bed and end with no wake-up, so you can stop listening whenever sleep comes.
On nights when words feel like too much, open Ambient sounds, choose waves or a mountain stream, and set the timer from 5 to 60 minutes. The sound fades out gently.
Download your favorite sessions once, choose your voice and a slower pace, then switch to airplane mode. In the morning, note any dream that stayed with you in your Dream Journal.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream to fall asleep?

Get into bed, turn off the lights and start Drifting into Sleep (16 minutes) or Sleep Journey (27 minutes). Don’t try to follow every word: if you fall asleep, the session simply ends without waking you. On nights when you’d rather hear no voice, play sleep sounds on the timer and let them fade out.
Should I choose a sleep meditation or sleep sounds?

Both have their place. A guided sleep meditation gives a busy mind something gentle to follow, like the weight of your body or the rhythm of your breath. Sleep sounds suit nights when words feel like too much. You can start with a voice, then switch to waves or a forest stream once you feel ready.
What if my mind keeps racing during a sleep meditation?

That’s normal, and it isn’t a failure. Each time you notice a thought, gently come back to what the voice describes, like the weight of your head on the pillow. Short practices help too: Your Instant Refuge or A Happy Memory Through Three Senses give your mind a pleasant place to rest before the lights go out.

02.seo: Stress Relief App: Breathing Exercises and 4-Minute Breaks
02.desc: Stress relief that fits your day: 4-minute breaks, breathing exercises and slow qigong for when everything moves too fast. No subscription, no ads, offline.
02.h1: How MeditaDream helps you reduce stress
02.accroche: Press pause, ease the overload and find steadier attention.
pitch: Stress relief shouldn’t require a free hour. The 4 Minutes sessions fit between two meetings: When Everything Moves Too Fast grounds you through your eyes, your feet and your breath, Relax Very Quickly loosens your body in three minutes, and Calming Down After an Argument helps the tension ease after a conflict.

When you have more time, breathing exercises take you deeper. Breathing with the Whole Body and The Luminous Breath calm your attention through the breath. Stabilizing Attention on the Breath — Ariadne’s Thread trains you to come back to it, again and again. And if sitting still is hard, The Dance of Qi — Qigong in Motion offers relaxation in slow motion.

Not sure where to start? Tell the Oracle how you feel and it suggests three meditations, or simply search “stress.” Set a daily reminder, download your favorite sessions, and your next break works anywhere, even offline. It’s all free, with no ads and no account.
etapes: When stress spikes, open the 4 Minutes category and play When Everything Moves Too Fast or Relax Very Quickly. Three or four minutes can be enough to come back to the present.
Tell the Oracle what’s going on, like “overwhelmed at work,” or type “stress” in the search bar to find sessions that match the moment.
Once a day, take a longer break: Breathing with the Whole Body (13 minutes), or a few rounds of box breathing over an ambient sound on the timer.
Set the meditation alarm for every day or chosen days, and download your favorite sessions so a calm break is always one tap away, even offline.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream for stress relief?

Start small. When stress rises, play a session from the 4 Minutes category, such as When Everything Moves Too Fast. Then build a habit: one longer breathing session a day, like The Luminous Breath, at a time set with the meditation alarm. If you’re unsure what fits, the Oracle suggests three meditations based on what you type.
What is box breathing, and can I practice it here?

Box breathing is a breathing exercise in four equal counts: breathe in for four, hold for four, breathe out for four, hold for four, as if tracing a square. The Learning library explains it step by step, and you can practice it on your own over an ambient sound on the timer. If holding your breath feels uncomfortable, simply skip the holds.
How long should I meditate to feel less stressed?

There’s no magic number. Three or four minutes can already help you step out of the rush, which is why the 4 Minutes sessions exist. Regularity matters more than length: a short daily session is easier to keep up than one long session a week. When you have more time, try a session of 13 to 25 minutes.

03.seo: Calm Anxiety With Meditation: A Free App for Worry and Fear
03.desc: Meditation for anxiety, at your pace: 4-minute anchors to calm anxiety in the moment, gentle sessions on fear and self-criticism. No subscription, no ads.
03.h1: How MeditaDream helps you calm anxiety
03.accroche: Look at worry, fear and self-criticism with gentler eyes: support for your well-being, never a replacement for care.
pitch: When worry takes over, you don’t need a lecture. You need something to hold on to. MeditaDream’s meditation for anxiety starts small: Your Instant Refuge brings a reassuring place to mind in four minutes, After Receiving Bad News pulls you back from worst-case scenarios, and When You Feel Watched or Judged separates facts from guesses about others.

Then you can look at fear itself, gently. Releasing Fear explores what your fear is trying to protect, while Fear of Failure and Fear of Judgment each take one worry at a time. Observing Thoughts — Watching the Trains Go by teaches you to let anxious thoughts pass instead of feeding them.

On low days, Daily Gratitude and When You Feel Like Giving Up offer a small step forward. Tell the Oracle how you feel to get three suggestions, or search “fear” to find the right session. Your Emotional Journal keeps track of the journey privately: there’s no account, and everything stays on your phone.
etapes: In the moment, open the Oracle and type what you feel, such as “knot in my stomach before work.” It suggests three meditations; a 4-minute one like Your Instant Refuge is a good first step.
When worries loop, play Observing Thoughts — Watching the Trains Go by. You practice noticing a thought, then letting it pass, like a train you don’t have to board.
Once a week, choose one fear and meet it calmly: Fear of Failure, Fear of Judgment or Releasing Fear. Slow the voice to 0.75× if a gentler pace feels better.
After each session, write a few words in your history or your Emotional Journal. Over the weeks, you’ll see which sessions help you most, privately, on your phone.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream to calm anxiety?

Use it in two ways. In the moment, a short session such as Your Instant Refuge or After Receiving Bad News helps you come back to the present. Over time, sessions like Releasing Fear or Welcoming a Difficult Emotion help you relate to worry differently. And when you don’t know where to start, the Oracle picks three meditations for how you feel.
What if meditating makes me more anxious?

It can happen, especially with eyes closed or long silences. Keep your eyes open, choose shorter sessions from the 4 Minutes category, and stop whenever you need to: nothing is forced. Anchoring in something concrete, like your feet on the floor or a sound in the room, often feels easier than following the breath.
Can MeditaDream replace professional support?

No. MeditaDream offers moments of calm and reflection for your well-being, but it does not replace a health professional. If anxiety or low moods last, feel overwhelming or get in the way of daily life, please talk to a health professional. If you ever feel in danger, contact emergency services right away. Meditation can sit alongside that support.

04.seo: Body Relaxation App: Guided Body Scan, Free and Offline
04.desc: A guided body scan, slow breathing and qigong for deep relaxation, from 3 to 30 minutes, to listen to your body at your own pace. No subscription, no ads.
04.h1: How MeditaDream helps you relax your body
04.accroche: Relax, breathe, listen to your body and build feel-good habits, with no health claims.
pitch: Busy days leave traces in your body: tight shoulders, a clenched jaw, shallow breathing. A body scan helps you notice it all, kindly. Body Scan — Mapping the Body from Within guides your attention through your body, one area at a time, and Relax Very Quickly loosens the main tension points in three minutes, sitting or standing.

For deeper relaxation, Breathing with the Whole Body connects breath and body, and The Body Under a Waterfall offers an imagined, sensory way to let go. If something feels sore, Breathing Around a Tender Spot explores discomfort gently, without forcing. Qigong lovers will find Warming the Hands, The Still Tree and The Small Circulation, a traditional loop of attention.

Make it a habit. Set a daily reminder, add a soft ambient sound, and read the illustrated lessons on posture and breathing in the Learning library. Your history keeps every session you’ve done, with room for your impressions. No ads, no account, and it all works offline.
etapes: Start with Body Scan — Mapping the Body from Within (17 minutes). Lie down or sit, and let the voice guide your attention through each part of your body, simply noticing what’s there.
Read the Learning library’s illustrated lessons on posture and breathing, so you can settle comfortably before longer sessions like Aligning the Seven Chakras (30 minutes).
Vary your relaxation through the week: Relax Very Quickly on busy days, The Body Under a Waterfall in the evening, The Dance of Qi — Qigong in Motion when you’d rather move.
Set the meditation alarm for chosen days, add waves or forest sounds, and after each session note how your body feels in your history.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream for body relaxation?

Make one body scan your base: Body Scan — Mapping the Body from Within, two or three times a week. On other days, try a short reset like Relax Very Quickly, or slow movement with The Dance of Qi — Qigong in Motion. Add an ambient sound, then note your impressions afterward to see what relaxes you most.
What is a body scan, and is it good for beginners?

A body scan means moving your attention slowly through your body, from one area to the next, simply noticing what you feel: warmth, tension or nothing at all. It’s one of the easiest ways to start meditating. In MeditaDream, Body Scan — Mapping the Body from Within is a 17-minute session made for beginners.
Can MeditaDream help with pain?

MeditaDream is a well-being app and does not replace a health professional. Breathing Around a Tender Spot invites you to approach discomfort gently, without forcing, and many people simply find relaxation pleasant. If you’re in pain or worried about your health, talk to a health professional first, and stop any exercise that doesn’t feel right.

05.seo: Emotional Balance App: Free Self-Compassion Meditations
05.desc: Find emotional balance with guided self-compassion, gratitude and forgiveness meditations, plus a private emotion journal. No subscription, no ads, offline.
05.h1: How MeditaDream helps you find emotional balance
05.accroche: Understand your reactions and grow gratitude, compassion and a kinder bond with yourself.
pitch: Emotional balance doesn’t mean never feeling angry or sad. It means making room for what you feel without being carried away. Welcoming a Difficult Emotion shows you how, and when a reaction runs hot, Calming Down After an Argument helps you step back in just three minutes.

Then comes a kinder inner voice. Developing Self-love and Compassion Meditation grow self-compassion, Releasing Comparison loosens the grip of comparing yourself to others, and Forgiving Yourself separates a mistake from who you are. For deeper work, Inner Child Serenity and Shadow Work gently look at what you usually avoid.

Gratitude steadies it all: Daily Gratitude and Precise Gratitude train you to notice what’s good. Write what you feel in your Emotional Journal or your Gratitude & Growth journal, privately, with no account. Unsure where to start today? The Oracle suggests three meditations for your mood, and a gentle reminder helps you keep going.
etapes: When an emotion runs high, open the Oracle, type what’s happening, like “angry after a call with my sister,” and choose one of its three suggestions.
Practice Welcoming a Difficult Emotion once a week, to make room for what you feel instead of fighting it. Calming Down After an Argument is there for heated moments.
Build self-compassion step by step: Developing Self-love, then Forgiving Yourself, then Inner Child Serenity. Set the meditation alarm so these sessions become a regular habit.
Each evening, write three lines in your Gratitude & Growth journal or your Emotional Journal. Your history also keeps your impressions after each session, private on your phone.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream to manage my emotions?

Combine three things: a session in the moment, a regular practice and a journal. Calming Down After an Argument helps when emotions run high. Welcoming a Difficult Emotion and Developing Self-love build steadier ground over time. And your Emotional Journal helps you understand your reactions. If you don’t know where to begin, ask the Oracle.
What is self-compassion?

Self-compassion means treating yourself the way you’d treat a good friend who’s struggling: with patience instead of harsh criticism. It isn’t self-pity, and it doesn’t mean ignoring your mistakes. You can practice it with Compassion Meditation (7 minutes) or Developing Self-love (15 minutes), and with Forgiving Yourself after a hard day.
Is it normal to feel emotional during a meditation?

Yes. Tears, irritation or sudden calm can all come up, especially in sessions like The Garden of Reunion or Shadow Work. You can pause, open your eyes or stop at any time. Afterward, a few lines in your journal can help you make sense of what came up, at your own pace.

06.seo: Spiritual Growth App: Third Eye, Chakras and Higher Self
06.desc: Explore spiritual awakening your way: chakras, the third eye, spirit guides and sacred places in 39 guided meditations. No subscription, no ads, offline.
06.h1: How MeditaDream helps you grow spiritually
06.accroche: Explore symbols, traditions, questions of meaning and inner experiences.
pitch: Spiritual awakening rarely comes in one leap. It grows from curiosity, practice and a few questions that won’t let go. MeditaDream gives you a map: Recognizing the Seven Chakras and Aligning the Seven Chakras guide you through the chakras, and the Third Eye sessions, such as The Inner Eye Awakens and The Door of Ajna, turn your attention inward.

Whether you picture a spirit guide, your higher self or simply your inner wisdom, The Guide of Light and The Council of Guides give it a face. Visit sacred places, from Beneath the Bodhi Tree to At the Center of Stonehenge, or learn from figures of wisdom in Sudhana’s Journey — The Teachers Along the Path.

Your inner journeys leave traces, so keep them. Describe your guides and their messages in the guides notebook, save the objects you bring back, and build your own sanctuaries. The zen passport marks each step of your path, with nothing to buy.
etapes: Start with the body as a map: Recognizing the Seven Chakras (27 minutes), then Aligning the Seven Chakras. Chakra Reset offers a slower, shorter way back whenever you need it.
Approach the third eye gently: The Third Eye and the Two Physical Eyes first, then The Inner Eye Awakens and The Image that Appears on its Own. These are advanced sessions, so take your time.
Meet your guides with The Ten Steps to the Temple of Light or The Guide of Light, then use your guides notebook to describe each guide, its message and when it returns.
Create a personal sanctuary, explore a world such as The Tree of Consciousness or The Cosmic Temple, and note signs and intuitions in your Spiritual Experiences journal.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream for spiritual growth?

Choose one thread and follow it for a few weeks: chakras, the third eye or spirit guides. Each thread has several sessions that build on one another. After each journey, write what you saw or felt in your journals or your guides notebook. Over time, those notes show how your path unfolds, and the zen passport marks the steps.
What is the third eye, and how do I start?

In yogic tradition, the third eye, or Ajna, is the sixth chakra, pictured between the eyebrows and linked to intuition and inner vision. MeditaDream approaches it as a way of turning attention inward and noticing inner images. Start with The Third Eye and the Two Physical Eyes, and don’t force anything: images may come, or they may not.
Do I need to believe in anything to use these meditations?

No. You can treat chakras, guides or your higher self as traditions, symbols or images for your imagination, and still enjoy the sessions as inner experiences. MeditaDream has no dogma and asks for no belief, only curiosity and a quiet moment. Take what speaks to you and leave the rest.

07.seo: Trance, Shamanism and Astral Travel: A Free Meditation App
07.desc: Explore astral projection, the shamanic journey and deep trance in 35 guided sessions, from micro-detachment to the rope technique. No subscription, no ads.
07.h1: How MeditaDream helps you explore trance, shamanism and astral travel
07.accroche: Explore inner states of consciousness, your imagination and the felt sense of leaving your body.
pitch: Astral projection fascinates many people, but few know where to begin. MeditaDream builds the path in stages. First, the Micro-Detachment sessions, like The Ceiling Magnet and The Point Behind Your Head, train small shifts of perception. Then the Astral Projection category takes over, with Astral · Floating Toward the Ceiling, Astral · Rope Technique and Astral · Imaginary Fall.

Drawn to ancestral traditions? The shamanic journey has its own sessions, like The Vision Quest, Journey to the Lower World and Journey to the Upper World. Progressive Descent into Trance and The 33-level Spiral take you deeper step by step, while Body Asleep, Mind Awake explores the threshold of sleep.

Everything here is experienced as an inner, subjective journey, and you stay in charge: open your eyes whenever you want. Create a sanctuary to start and end each trip, note the guides you meet in the guides notebook, and keep the objects you bring back. Downloaded sessions play offline, so nothing breaks the trance.
etapes: Begin with micro-detachment: The Ceiling Magnet, The Tiny Shift and The Slide. Lie down and explore imagined sensations of rising or sliding, 16 to 19 minutes at a time.
Then follow the astral projection sessions, from Astral · Floating Toward the Ceiling to Astral · Rope Technique, when you’re rested and know you won’t be disturbed.
For a shamanic journey, start with The Circle of Protection to build a safe inner space, then try Journey to the Lower World or The Vision Quest.
Afterward, note the guides you met in your guides notebook and the objects you found in your collection. Add an ambient sound and download your sessions, so nothing interrupts you.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream to practice astral projection?

Go step by step. Start with the Micro-Detachment category, which trains small, imagined shifts of perception, then follow the Astral Projection sessions, from Astral · Floating Toward the Ceiling to Astral · The Target. Practice lying down, rested, at a quiet time. Astral · Target to Verify even invites you to check your impressions afterward.
What is a shamanic journey?

In many traditions, a shamanic journey is an inner voyage, often to the beat of a drum, toward a lower world, an upper world or the presence of ancestors. MeditaDream offers it as a guided, imaginary journey, with sessions like Journey to the Lower World and The Vision Quest. You bring back images and insights to reflect on.
Is trance or astral projection safe for beginners?

These sessions are guided, imaginary experiences, and you can open your eyes and stop at any time. Most are marked advanced, so begin with shorter ones like The Ceiling Magnet. Avoid them when you’re exhausted, need to stay alert or feel emotionally fragile, and never listen while driving.

Five to fifteen minutes is plenty at first. What counts is coming back often, ideally every day, rather than sitting for a long time once in a while. On the body side, qigong starts with your hands. Warming the Hands draws attention to the sensations in your palms, The Still Tree trains a stable, relaxed stance, and The Dance of Qi — Qigong in Motion links breath and slow gestures. Later, The Small Circulation follows a traditional qigong path of attention. No class or equipment needed.

For a zen meditation mood, sit in The Zen Garden or Monastery at Sunrise, or contemplate the place of the Buddha’s awakening in Beneath the Bodhi Tree. Illustrated lessons explain posture and breathing, ambient sounds set the scene, and your journals keep what you discover.

What’s the difference between zen meditation, vipassana and qigong?

Zen meditation, rooted in Chan and Japanese Buddhism, centers on sitting and simply being present. Vipassana, from the Theravada tradition, trains you to watch sensations change, moment by moment. Qigong is a Chinese practice that joins breath, posture and slow movement. In MeditaDream, you can practice qigong with four guided sessions and explore Buddhist wisdom through eight guided meditations.
Do I need to be Buddhist to practice?

Not at all. These meditations use Buddhist figures and Taoist landscapes as symbols and sources of wisdom, and they ask for no religious commitment. You can approach them with curiosity, the way you’d visit a temple while traveling. Qigong, too, is open to everyone: you only need a little space and a few quiet minutes.

Creativity needs a freer mind. Creative Unblocking invites you to set your inner critic aside, Directed Waking Dream sparks unexpected associations, and The Unknown Planet feeds your curiosity. What is mindfulness, exactly?

Mindfulness means paying attention, on purpose, to what’s happening right now, like your breath, a sound or a thought, without judging it. It’s the foundation of most meditation for focus. You can practice it seated with Observing Thoughts — Watching the Trains Go by, or in daily life with Meditating with Your Eyes Open — Staying Present in the Midst of the World.
Can meditation really boost creativity?

Meditation won’t write your novel, but it can create the conditions ideas need: a calmer mind and less self-judgment. Creative Unblocking invites you to suspend your inner critic, and Directed Waking Dream lets images and associations flow. Keep a notebook nearby, or use your history, to catch what comes up after the session.

Then go deeper. Developing Self-love builds a kinder inner voice, Releasing Comparison puts distance between you and other people’s lives, and Fear of Failure reminds you that a mistake doesn’t define your worth. What’s the difference between self-confidence and self-love?

Self-confidence is trust in what you can do; self-love is how you treat yourself, whatever you achieve. The second makes the first easier: when a mistake doesn’t shake your worth, you dare to try again. That’s why this page pairs Developing Self-love and Forgiving Yourself with action-focused sessions like When You Lack Motivation.
What if I don’t feel motivated to meditate?

Start smaller than you think. When You Lack Motivation lasts three minutes and helps you find one doable first step, and When You Feel Like Giving Up separates a tired moment from a real decision. Set a gentle reminder, and let your dragon’s growth show you that every minute counts.

pitch: Lucid dreaming starts before you fall asleep. Lucid Dream Preparation helps you set the intention to recognize that you’re dreaming, and Body Asleep, Mind Awake explores that strange threshold where the body rests and the mind stays awake. The Image that Appears on its Own trains you to watch the pictures that rise by themselves, just as they do in dreams.

In the morning, your dream journal takes over. Write down your dreams, their symbols and the ones that keep coming back. Over time, you may start to recognize your own dream signs, the clues that tell you you’re dreaming. Your journals stay private, on your phone, with no account.

Not every night has to be an exploration. When you simply want rest, Drifting into Sleep and Sleep Journey guide you into sleep without seeking lucidity. Add a soft ambient sound, choose a slower voice, and download everything so it plays in airplane mode.

faq: How do I use MeditaDream for lucid dreaming?

Use it at two moments. At night, Lucid Dream Preparation sets the intention to recognize your dreams, and Body Asleep, Mind Awake explores the edge of sleep. In the morning, write everything you remember in the Dream Journal, and reread it to spot recurring dream signs. Lucid dreams can take weeks to come, so give it time.
Why keep a dream journal?

Dreams fade within minutes of waking. Writing them down right away tends to help you remember more of them over time, and your notes reveal the places, people and symbols that come back. Those recurring dream signs are what many lucid dreamers learn to notice. In MeditaDream, the Dream Journal is private and stays on your phone.
Can lucid dreaming practice disturb my sleep?

Lucid Dream Preparation is best kept for nights when you want to explore your dreams, not for falling asleep quickly. When rest comes first, choose Drifting into Sleep or Sleep Journey instead. If exploring your dreams leaves you tired, take a break for a few nights and come back to it later.

13.h1: How MeditaDream helps you grieve, forgive and let go
13.accroche: A personal space for reflection in times of loss or change.
pitch: Grief has no timetable, and no meditation can rush it. What MeditaDream offers is a quiet space to be with what you feel. The Garden of Reunion invites you to explore words left unsaid, My Departed Animal honors the memory of a pet who’s gone, and Welcoming a Difficult Emotion makes room for sadness and anger.

Forgiveness comes at its own pace, and it’s never an obligation. Forgiving Without Forgetting looks at resentment without forcing you to forgive, Forgiving Yourself works gently with guilt, and Heart-Centered Ho’oponopono uses repeated phrases to support reflection. For letting go, The Forest of Thorns explores how you face what stands in your way.

Some days call for a refuge. Create your own sanctuary, write in your journals what you can’t say out loud, and let the Oracle suggest three meditations for how you feel today. There’s no account, and everything stays private on your phone.
etapes: Begin softly: tell the Oracle what you’re going through, like “I miss my father,” and choose one of its three suggestions, or start with the seven-minute Compassion Meditation.

Approach forgiveness step by step: Forgiving Without Forgetting first, then Forgiving Yourself or Heart-Centered Ho’oponopono, at your own pace and only if you wish.
Create a personal sanctuary, a safe inner place to return to, and write in your journals after each session. Everything stays private, on your phone.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream when I’m grieving?

Go at your own pace. Short, gentle sessions like Compassion Meditation can keep you company on hard days. When you feel ready, The Garden of Reunion and My Departed Animal offer a space to remember and say what was left unsaid. Writing in your journals afterward can help too, and the Oracle can suggest three meditations for today.
Do I have to forgive in order to let go?

No. Letting go doesn’t require forgiving, and forgiving doesn’t mean forgetting or excusing what happened. Forgiving Without Forgetting explores resentment without imposing forgiveness, and The Forest of Thorns looks at how you face what hurts. Some people find forgiveness along the way; others simply find more peace. Both are valid.
Can MeditaDream replace support during grief?

No. MeditaDream offers a personal space for reflection, but it does not replace a health professional or the people close to you. If your grief feels overwhelming, lasts a long time or makes daily life hard, please reach out to a health professional or a support group. Meditation can sit alongside that help, never instead of it.
